key_insight: Raising argon flow from 1600 to 1800 L/h during air plasma spraying makes NiCrFeBSiC coatings thicker, denser, and more wear resistant.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing plasma spray gas flow can improve coating quality and adhesion for protective surface engineering applications.
method: Air plasma sprayed self-fluxing NiCrFeBSiC metal-ceramic coatings.
Compared argon flow rates of 1600 vs 1800 L/h during deposition.
Evaluated structure, microhardness, elastic modulus, scratch adhesion, and ball-on-disk tribology.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports about a twofold increase in coating thickness, a twofold drop in porosity, microhardness of 1015.8 ± 81.5 HV, elastic modulus of 203.9 ± 5.4 GPa, and a lower friction coefficient at 1800 L/h (≈0.107).
watch_item: The study compares only two argon flow settings, so broader process windows and long-term wear behavior still need validation.
paper_title: EFFECT OF ARGON FLOW RATE DURING AIR PLASMA SPRAYING ON THE STRUCTURE AND PROPERTIES OF NICRFEBSIC COATINGS
